source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Login to OpenBMC Web GUI: Open a browser and enter the IP address or hostname of the target OpenBMC server to access the Web GUI. Sign in with your login credentials.
2. Find User Management Options: Once logged in, look for options related to user management. This may be found in the User Accounts, Permissions, Authentication, etc. sections.
3. Set up users: In the user management area, you can create, edit or manage user accounts. Make sure that the user account you set has appropriate permissions for subsequent setting operations.

4. Look for Zeroconf or Network settings: In OpenBMC's Web GUI, look for options related to Zeroconf or Network settings. This may be found in sections such as network settings, connectivity, or system settings.

5. Enable Zeroconf or mDNS: In Zeroconf or Network Settings, look for an option to enable Zeroconf or mDNS. This may have a switch or option that lets you enable Zeroconf or mDNS functionality.

6.Save Settings: After making a setting change, make sure to save the settings.

7. Restart service or system (if required): In some cases, configuration changes may require restarting network services or the OpenBMC system to apply the changes. Please refer to the relevant documentation to determine if this is required.

8 .Test Zeroconf: When you're done with the setup, other Zeroconf-capable devices should be able to discover your OpenBMC server on the same LAN.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
If your BMC or server hostname is myserver, then you can enter http://myserver.local
On Linux systems that support mDNS, you can use the avahi-browse command to view the Zeroconf device list

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Zeroconf discoverable through systemd-networkd: confirm the BMC/server hostname is discoverable as http://${BMC_HOSTNAME:?operator must set the bmc server hostname for mDNS}.local (mDNS). Agent can check the mDNS/Zeroconf visibility from the client sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "avahi-browse -rt _http._tcp 2>&1 | grep -Ei '= .*_http|hostname' | head -n 30; systemctl is-active avahi-daemon 2>&1" ; needs avahi/zeroconf set up on the BMC side.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the avahi-browse Zeroconf entries so the operator confirms <host>.local resolves to the BMC/server.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; usable discovery concept but unsafe credential/SSH wrapper.

original_test_intent: Enable the BMC's Zeroconf/mDNS advertisement and prove that the intended hostname and HTTP service are discoverable and resolvable on the same LAN.
original_method: An authorized user enables mDNS in WebUI, then a Linux peer uses hostname.local and avahi-browse to discover the BMC.
manual_activity: Engineer approves or performs the WebUI configuration and any BMC network restart; client discovery, resolution and evidence capture can be automated.
safety_requirements: Protect credentials and verify management identity; no sshpass or disabled host-key validation.
Avoid unintended user/account changes beyond the approved prerequisite.
Maintain alternate management access before network restart.
No automatic retry; restore prior mDNS policy after test if required.
agent_execution_scope: From the approved client, query mDNS/DNS-SD, resolve A/AAAA, connect to the advertised endpoint and correlate identity.
Do not change BMC users/network without approval or issue verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve/apply BMC mDNS configuration and restart if required.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: avahi-browse is relevant; the embedded-password SSH wrapper and disabled host-key verification are rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run client-side avahi-browse/resolution with protected credentials and verify the endpoint certificate/identity.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: WebUI enablement, hostname.local, avahi-browse and 10/10 minutes remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture BMC config, enable the approved mDNS service, discover from a same-L2 client, resolve hostname, validate service/port/identity, then restore policy.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: BMC mDNS implementation and routed/VLAN policy.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC, systemd-networkd/mDNS and client Avahi versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BMC network and mDNS/DNS-SD documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity, service-record and rollback evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Preserves discovery while excluding spoofed/wrong responder success.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: mDNS normally does not cross L2 boundaries.

project_override_considerations: Project may choose a different allowed hostname/service set, but must record the actual interface and service coverage.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, procedure and criteria consistently target Zeroconf/mDNS; systemd-networkd versus WebUI implementation detail requires platform confirmation, not a policy contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Configuration, package and hostname are ordinary inputs; the discovery core is automatable after approval.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains Avahi but rejects unsafe SSH/credential handling.

review_improvement: Prevents a different mDNS responder or stale record from satisfying the BMC discovery case.
independent_technical_reasoning: Discovery queries, name resolution and endpoint correlation are deterministic software operations; only BMC configuration/restart authority requires engineer involvement.
